correctness.rationale: For one Rademacher probe, \(D_i=z_i(Hz)_i=H_{ii}+\sum_{j\ne i}H_{ij}z_iz_j\); orthogonality of distinct Rademacher monomials gives mean \(H_{ii}\) and variance \(\sum_{j\ne i}H_{ij}^2\). Independent probe averaging divides only the variance by \(m\). The bias-corrected RMS-square is a convex combination of identically distributed squared estimates whose weights sum to one, giving the exact time-independent expectation. In two dimensions, writing one coordinate's squared projection onto the small-eigenvalue eigenspace as \(p\) reduces the squared inflation to a one-variable rational function with unique maximum at \(p=\kappa/(\kappa+1)\), giving the claimed sharp factor and its \(m\)-probe version. Fresh exhaustive Rademacher enumeration for several random symmetric matrices and independent evaluation of the condition-number maximizer reproduced the formulas.
correctness.risk: The result is for a fixed Hessian, block size one, and expected RMS square rather than expected RMS.

value.rationale: AdaHessian explicitly uses RMS smoothing and spatial averaging to manage stochastic Hessian-diagonal noise. The theorem identifies a persistent, exact consequence of that design: off-diagonal curvature becomes the RMS mean-square target, quantifies its worst conditioning distortion, and shows precisely how multiple probes suppress it. That is a motivated optimizer-structure invariant rather than a bare estimator variance calculation.
value.risk: The theorem does not address changing Hessians, spatial blocks larger than one, or full optimizer convergence.

final_claim: For paper-form AdaHessian on a fixed quadratic without spatial averaging, averaging \(m\) independent Rademacher Hutchinson probes before the Hessian RMS gives \(\mathbb E[\overline D_{t,i}^{\,2}]=H_{ii}^2+m^{-1}\sum_{j\ne i}H_{ij}^2\) at every time; for one probe the target is the squared row norm, and in two dimensions the sharp RMS inflation over all SPD orientations of condition number \(\kappa\) is \((\kappa+1)/(2\sqrt\kappa)\), with the stated exact \(m\)-probe reduction.
limitations: Fixed deterministic quadratic Hessian and no spatial averaging.
Expected squared RMS state only; no claim for expected RMS or almost-sure convergence.
The sharp condition-number envelope is two-dimensional.
